alternatives.root_cause: Cart's valkey datastore became slow or saturated
alternatives.why_not: The ~300ms penalty is identical across valkey commands and the unrelated flagd HTTP call, which a store-side problem would not explain; and flagd itself answers in 0.1ms.

alternatives.root_cause: flagd was slow and cart blocked on flag evaluation
alternatives.why_not: flagd's own spans are ~0.1ms; the 300ms sits in cart's client-side POST span before flagd is reached.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart was cut off from the network
alternatives.why_not: Cart reaches valkey and flagd successfully on every call and logs no unreachability; traffic is delayed, not dropped.

alternatives.root_cause: A configuration value on cart was edited to the wrong timeout or address
alternatives.why_not: The change record shows a sidecar network-shaping container, not an edit to any cart configuration value; the mechanism in play is injected latency on the call path.

verdict.summary: A traffic-shaping container attached to cart's network namespace at 00:23 injected a 300ms delay on eth0, so every cart outbound call (valkey HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE and flagd) pays ~300ms and checkout/frontend requests stretch to seconds.
verdict.reasoning: Cart's own error ratio is flat at zero and its log is continuous and healthy (tr_77b42b675c4d, tr_66d7729de4c0), so cart is not erroring or frozen - it is slow. Traces (tr_ad46a5173ed3) show a uniform ~300ms self-time on each of cart's outbound hops (HGET, HMSET, EXPIRE, the flagd POST) while flagd, product-catalog, currency, payment, shipping and email all respond in single-digit milliseconds; the delay is therefore added per network operation inside cart's namespace rather than caused by any downstream service. The change log (tr_8f53cea1c696) records a traffic-shaping container attached to cart's network namespace at 00:23:06 with eth0 delay=300ms, just before onset at 00:27:46. Checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator alert because they wait on cart's EmptyCart/GetCart path; they are the callers, not the fault. Remediation is to remove that injected delay, i.e. revert the shaping change.
open_questions: Why the traffic-shaping container was attached (deliberate experiment vs. misapplied automation) is not settled by the change record.
Whether the alerting services failed on deadline/timeout errors or merely on latency thresholds was not checked - no checkout/frontend error-ratio series was pulled.
Whether other services in the blast radius share the same shaping container was not observed.
